transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I... well, I keep blowing up at people over absolutely nothing. I work in retail, and the other day I just yelled at one of my employees for putting stock on the wrong shelf. Afterward, I was literally shaking, because... that is just not how I usually treat people. It really scared me, and I need to figure out what's going on.
How often have you been having these kinds of angry outbursts?

It feels like it's happening a lot lately. Like I said, I just keep blowing up at people over absolutely nothing. That time with my employee and the stock shelf was probably the worst one, which is why I was shaking so much afterward. But just generally snapping at people... it's almost every day right now. It's just really not how I normally treat people, and it's exhausting.
Apart from feeling angry, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or depressed lately?
No, not really. I mean, I'm definitely stressed out and on edge, but I wouldn't say I feel sad or depressed. It's more just this constant frustration and anger that I can't seem to shake.
Have you ever had periods lasting a few days where you felt unusually energetic, wired, or hyperactive?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I'm just feeling really tense and irritable all the time, not energetic or hyper.
Did these outbursts and irritability start after a specific stressful event or major life change?

Yeah, it did. This has all been going on for about two weeks now. It started right after... well, there was a kitchen fire during our first weekend working on the house. Ever since that happened, I've just been like this.
Have you been having unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about the kitchen fire?

Yeah, I have. The fire just keeps jumping into my head out of nowhere. I'll just be doing something normal, like... picking up a pan, or even just opening a spreadsheet at work, and suddenly I’m right back there. I can actually smell the smoke and see the kitchen filling up before I can even stop it from happening.
Just to clarify the timeline, has it been more than a month since the fire and the start of these symptoms?

No, not a month. Like I mentioned a minute ago, it's only been about two weeks. It's been going on exactly since that kitchen fire happened during our first weekend working on the house. So, yeah, just two weeks.
